sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Alend is an Irish goddess. The old capital Almu carried her name. That city ruled the eastern province of Leinster. The hill where it once stood is the Hill of Allen today. It lies in County Kildare. Her name also marks the wide Bog of Allen. People personified the hill as Almu, which means all white. A hidden door to the Otherworld stood on the hill. King Nuada held it first. The hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill seized it from Nuada by force. The hill was named his birthplace. A small mound on top was his seat. Some confuse Almu with Knockaulin.

okr.objective: Describe Alend, the Irish goddess who gave her name to the Bog of Allen.
key_results: Alend was a royal and heroic Irish goddess.
Her name marked the old capital Almu.
The Hill of Allen and the Bog of Allen carry her name.
The hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill took the hill by force.
